prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing/matching that operates on the raw header string without properly tokenizing per RFC 7235 auth-param syntax, causing incorrect matches when commas appear inside quoted values or when scheme names are matched as substrings. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing/matching that operates on the raw header string without properly tokenizing per RFC 7235 auth-param syntax, causing incorrect matches when commas appear inside quoted values or when scheme names are matched as substrings. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041 splits the entire header into top-level comma-separated challenge segments first (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and then matches the scheme via segment.partition(' ') before extracting Bearer's params (_extract_bearer_auth_params), which correctly handles headers containing multiple auth schemes (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...') without misidentifying scheme boundaries. PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only finds the first space in the whole header and then comma-splits everything after it as params, so it does not distinguish a second scheme's name from a continued param list when multiple challenges are present in one header — a narrower fix for the same quoted-comma parsing problem.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py eagerly runs json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values for str-containing union types (most commonly `str | None`) whenever the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. the literal text "null", "true", or "123" gets silently decoded into None/bool/int instead of being kept as the intended string). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py eagerly runs json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values for str-containing union types (most commonly `str | None`) whenever the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. the literal text "null", "true", or "123" gets silently decoded into None/bool/int instead of being kept as the intended string). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs edit the exact same `if isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` guard in pre_parse_json and can't both land. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` disables pre-parsing for ANY union composed entirely of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. it also turns off pre-parsing for `int | float | None`, which regresses the existing (and still needed) behavior of decoding stringified numbers into int/float for those fields. #2032 also compares union members directly against a type frozenset without unwrapping `Annotated`, so it fails to detect the extremely common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` shape and leaves that case unfixed. #3056's `_is_optional_str` scopes the skip narrowly to str-only unions (the only case where pre-parsing can corrupt data) and explicitly unwraps `Annotated` via a dedicated helper, so it fixes the corruption bug for the Annotated+Optional[str] pattern used throughout mcpserver tool signatures without touching numeric-union parsing behavior.

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs edit the exact same `if isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` guard in pre_parse_json and can't both land. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` disables pre-parsing for ANY union composed entirely of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. it also turns off pre-parsing for `int | float | None`, which regresses the existing (and still needed) behavior of decoding stringified numbers into int/float for those fields. #2032 also compares union members directly against a type frozenset without unwrapping `Annotated`, so it fails to detect the extremely common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` shape and leaves that case unfixed. #3056's `_is_optional_str` scopes the skip narrowly to str-only unions (the only case where pre-parsing can corrupt data) and explicitly unwraps `Annotated` via a dedicated helper, so it fixes the corruption bug for the Annotated+Optional[str] pattern used throughout mcpserver tool signatures without touching numeric-union parsing behavior.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 splits the entire header into top-level comma-separated challenge segments first (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and then matches the scheme via segment.partition(' ') before extracting Bearer's params (_extract_bearer_auth_params), which correctly handles headers containing multiple auth schemes (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...') without misidentifying scheme boundaries. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the exact same `if isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` guard in pre_parse_json and can't both land. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` disables pre-parsing for ANY union composed entirely of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. it also turns off pre-parsing for `int | float | None`, which regresses the existing (and still needed) behavior of decoding stringified numbers into int/float for those fields. #2032 also compares union members directly against a type frozenset without unwrapping `Annotated`, so it fails to detect the extremely common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` shape and leaves that case unfixed. #3056's `_is_optional_str` scopes the skip narrowly to str-only unions (the only case where pre-parsing can corrupt data) and explicitly unwraps `Annotated` via a dedicated helper, so it fixes the corruption bug for the Annotated+Optional[str] pattern used throughout mcpserver tool signatures without touching numeric-union parsing behavior.
